title: Sequence Scout: interactive span sequencing & correlation panel
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Engineers struggle to quickly understand request causality when multiple parallel spans and fallback model routes are present. Existing trace views require hunting across panes and often lose correlation context (e.g., cross-region fallbacks or batched KV cache hits).

Goal: Design an integrated panel, "Sequence Scout", that lets engineers compactly inspect ordered span sequences, surface correlated request IDs, highlight fallbacks and model variant switches, and offer lightweight filtering and jump-to-request flows for the Redwood Console. The panel should be usable as a detachable side-panel and embedded in request drilldowns.

Proposed solution summary: Sequence Scout shows a condensed vertical timeline of span sequences (primary path + secondary branches). Each row is a span-summary card with micro-metrics (latency, GPU type, batch size) and a compact icon for special behaviours (cache hit, quantized execution, fallback). Correlation IDs are pinned at the top with copy/expand behavior. A scrubber allows stepping through the sequence; selecting a span expands an inline waterfall with logs, model variant metadata and request headers. Filters support boolean combinations (e.g., model_variant:>redwood-v2 AND cache_hit:false).

Success metrics: reduce median triage time by 30% in pilot, enable FTO (first-time-observer) to find root cause without leaving the panel in 60% of cases, and maintain 90th-percentile render time < 200ms for traces up to 250 spans.

Constraints and non-goals: not intended to replace full trace replay or session export. Will support up to 500 spans in the initial design; heavy-duty replay and debugging remain separate features. Accessibility: ensure keyboard navigation and ARIA labels for scrubber and span cards. Mobile: secondary priority, desktop-first UX.
decisions: Use vertical condensed sequence as default rather than horizontal waterfall to optimize for tall dashboards and side-panels
Show correlation ID as a persistent header with quick copy and timeline anchoring
Inline waterfall on-demand to avoid overwhelming users on initial load; lazy-load detailed logs and model metadata
Expose a filter bar supporting boolean operators and saved filters (prototype only; persistence for later cycles)
tradeoffs: Condensed vertical layout sacrifices some timing visual fidelity vs full-width waterfall but improves multi-trace comparison in dashboards
Lazy-loading logs reduces initial render time at the cost of an additional network roundtrip when expanding spans
Supporting complex boolean filter syntax increases learning curve but provides powerful triage capabilities for SREs
